steps.say: Rocks are natural, hard materials that make up the Earth. Different rocks have different properties.

figure.alt: A rock, a stone and a mountain.

steps.say: Granite is hard and chalk is soft. Some rocks let water soak in, and some do not.
Soil is tiny bits of rock mixed with humus, which is rotted plants and animals. Soil also holds air and water.

figure.alt: Soil, an earthworm and a dead leaf.

steps.say: Sandy soil has big grains, so water drains quickly. Clay soil has tiny bits, so it holds water.
steps.show: sandy: drains fast. clay: holds water.

steps.say: A fossil is the remains of a living thing from long ago, kept in rock.
Fossils form when a living thing is buried in mud or sand. The layers slowly turn into rock.

check.prompt: Which soil holds on to water best?

options.why: Sandy soil has big gaps, so water drains away quickly.
Gravel has big gaps, so water runs straight through.
Sand lets water drain away fast.

hints: Water drains through gaps in soil.
Which soil feels sticky when wet?
check.explanation: Clay soil has very tiny bits packed closely, so water drains slowly. It holds on to water.

check.prompt: The remains of a living thing from long ago, kept in rock, is called a ___.
hints: Scientists dig these out of rock.
Dinosaur bones in museums are an example.
check.explanation: A fossil is the remains or shape of an ancient living thing kept in rock.
